35:10: God the Almighty commanded His believing servants who are pure in religion and in person to banish the polytheists who are impure in religion from the Sacred Mosque and not to approach it after the revelation of this verse. It was revealed in the year nine, and for this reason the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) sent Ali with Abu Bakr may God be pleased with them both that year and commanded him to announce to the polytheists that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year and no one should circumambulate the House naked. So God completed that and decreed it by law and destiny. Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say about the words of God the Almighty: The polytheists are impure, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs unless he is a slave or one of the People of the Covenant. It was narrated from another chain of transmission, and Imam Ahmad said: Hussain told us, Sharik told us, from Al-Ash'ath, meaning Ibn Suwar, from Al-Hasan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No polytheist will enter our mosque after this year of ours except the people of the covenant and their servants. Imam Ahmad alone transmitted it from the Prophet, and the Mawquf narration is more authentic in its chain of transmission. Imam Abu Amr Al-Awza'i said: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, wrote to prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims, and he followed his prohibition with the words of God, the Most High: The polytheists are unclean. Ata' said: The entire Haram is a mosque, because God, the Most High, said: So let them not approach Al-Masjid Al-Haram after this year of theirs. This noble verse indicates the impurity of the polytheist, as mentioned in the Sahih: The believer does not become impure. As for the impurity of his body, the majority are of the view that he is not impure in body and soul, because God, the Most High, permitted the food of the People of the Book. Some of the Zahiris held that their bodies are impure. Ash'ath said from Al-Hasan: Whoever shakes hands with them should perform ablution. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And His statement, And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: This is because the people said that the markets will be cut off from us, trade will be destroyed, and the amenities we used to gain from them will be taken away from us. So God revealed, And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, from another source, If He wills, until His statement, while they are humbled, meaning this is in exchange for what you feared from the cutting off of those markets. So God compensated them for what He had cut off from the matter of polytheism by giving them from the necks of the People of the Book the jizya. And thus it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and others: Indeed, God is Knowing, meaning what is good for you, Wise, meaning in what He commands and forbids, because He is perfect in His actions and words, just in His creation and command, blessed and exalted be He. For this reason, He compensated them for those earnings with the jizya money that they take from the People of the Covenant. And the Almighty said: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah with willing submission while they are subdued.” In fact, when they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they no longer had true faith in any of the messengers or in what they brought. Rather, they follow their opinions, their whims, and their fathers in what they are doing, not because it is the law of God and His religion. Because if they had true faith in what they had in their hands, it would have led them to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because all the prophets gave glad tidings of him and commanded them to follow him. But when he came and they disbelieved in him, and he is the most honorable of messengers, it was known that they were not adhering to the law of the earlier prophets because it is from God. Rather, it is their luck and their whims, so their belief in the rest of the prophets does not benefit them, and they disbelieved in their master, the best of them, the last of them, and the most perfect of them. That is why He said: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture.” This noble verse is the first command to fight the People of the Book after the affairs of the polytheists were prepared and people entered the religion of God in droves and the Arabian Peninsula was set straight. God and His Messenger commanded to fight the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. That was in the year nine. That is why the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prepared to fight the Romans and called the people to that and showed it to them. He sent to the Arab tribes around Medina and urged them, so they prepared with him and about thirty thousand fighters gathered, and some people from the people of Medina and those around it from the hypocrites and others stayed behind. That was in a year of drought and a time of intense heat and scorching sun. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out intending to go to Syria to fight the Romans, so he reached Tabuk and settled there and stayed there for about twenty days. Then he sought God’s guidance in returning, so he returned. This is generally due to the straitened circumstances and the weakness of the people, as will be explained later, God willing. This noble verse has been used as evidence by those who believe that the jizya should only be taken from the People of the Book or those similar to them, such as the Magians, as is authentically reported in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from the Magians of Hajar. This is the view of al-Shafi’i and Ahmad, according to the well-known view of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him. Rather, it should be taken from all non-Arabs, whether they are People of the Book or polytheists, and it should not be taken from the Arabs except from the People of the Book. Imam Malik said: Rather, it is permissible to impose the jizya on all infidels, whether they are people of the Book, Zoroastrian, pagan, or others. The sources of these doctrines and the mention of their evidence are not mentioned in this place, and God knows best. And his saying: Until they pay the jizyah means if they do not submit by hand meaning by force and domination while they are humiliated meaning humiliated, despised and disgraced. Therefore, it is not permissible to honor the People of the Covenant or raise them above the Muslims. Rather, they are humiliated, despised and miserable, as came in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not initiate the greeting of peace with the Jews and Christians, and if you meet one of them on the road, force him to its narrowest part.” For this reason, the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, imposed on them those well-known conditions in humiliating, belittling and degrading them. This is what the imams and preservers of hadith narrated from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim al-Ash’ari, who said: I wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, when he made peace with the Christians of the people of Ash-Sham: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is a letter from Abdullah Umar, the Commander of the Faithful, from the Christians of such-and-such city. When you came to us, we asked you for safety for ourselves, our children, our wealth and the people of our religion, and we stipulated for you upon ourselves that we would not incite any evil in our city. Nor shall we have a monastery, church, cell, or monk’s cell around it, nor shall we renew what has been destroyed in it, nor shall we revive what was planned for the Muslims, nor shall we prevent any Muslim from entering our churches, day or night, nor shall we widen their doors for passersby and wayfarers, nor shall we provide food for any Muslim who passes by us for three days, nor shall we shelter a spy in our churches or homes, nor shall we conceal any deception from the Muslims, nor shall we teach our children the Qur’an, nor shall we display polytheism, nor call anyone to it, nor shall we prevent any of our relatives from entering Islam if they wish to do so, nor shall we respect the Muslims, nor shall we stand up for them from our gatherings if they wish to sit, nor shall we resemble them in any of their clothing, in a skullcap, turban, sandals, or parting of the hair, nor shall we speak their language, nor shall we adopt their nicknames, nor shall we ride saddles, nor gird ourselves with swords, nor shall we take any weapon, nor carry it with us, nor engrave our rings in Arabic, nor shall we sell alcohol, nor shall we cut the front of our heads, nor shall we adhere to our dress wherever we are, nor shall we tie our belts on our heads, nor shall we be afraid of the evil... Our midst and that we do not display the cross on our churches and that we do not display our crosses or our books in any of the roads or markets of the Muslims and that we do not ring our bells in our churches except lightly and that we do not raise our voices in reading in our churches in any of the presence of the Muslims and that we do not go out to the palm groves or the ba’oth and that we do not raise our voices with our dead and do not display fires with them in any of the roads or markets of the Muslims and that we do not live with them with our dead and that we do not take from the slaves what the arrows of the Muslims have been made upon and that we guide the Muslims and do not spy on them in their homes. He said: So when I brought the letter to Omar, he added to it and we do not strike any of the Muslims. We stipulated that for you on ourselves and the people of our religion and we accepted security on it. If we contradicted anything of what we stipulated for you and imposed on ourselves, then we have no covenant and what is permissible for you from us is permissible from the people of opposition and discord. God Almighty often uses as evidence for the Resurrection His revival of the earth after its death, as in the beginning of Surat Al-Hajj, He reminds His servants to consider this, for the earth is dead and lifeless, with no vegetation on it. Then, when He sends clouds to it carrying water and sends it down upon it, it quivers and swells and grows [abundantly] of every beautiful pair. Likewise, when God Almighty wants to resurrect and raise bodies, He sends down rain from beneath the Throne that covers the entire earth, and the bodies grow in their graves as a seed grows in the earth. For this reason, it is stated in the Sahih, Every son of Adam decays except the coccyx; from it he was created and from it he will be rebuilt. For this reason, God Almighty said, Such is the Resurrection. In Al-Hajj, the hadith of Abu Razin was mentioned. I said, O Messenger of God, how does God bring the dead back to life? What is the sign of that in His creation? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, O Abu Razin, have you not passed by a barren valley of your people, then passed by it quivering with greenery? I said, Yes. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, That is how God brings people back to life. The dead And the Almighty said: Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor. That is, whoever wants to be honored in this world and the Hereafter, let him adhere to obeying God, the Most High, for he will achieve his goal because God, the Most High, is the Owner of this world and the Hereafter, and to Him belongs all honor, as God, the Most High, said: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers - do they seek honor with them? But indeed, all honor belongs to God. And the Almighty said: “And let not their statement grieve you. Indeed, all honor belongs to God.” And the Almighty said: To God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know. Mujahid said: Whoever desires honor by worshipping idols, to God belongs all honor. Qatadah said: Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor, that is, let him be honored by obeying God, the Most High. It was said: Whoever desires knowledge of whose honor belongs, then to God belongs all honor. Ibn Jarir narrated this. And the words of God Almighty: To Him ascends the good words, meaning remembrance, recitation, and supplication. This was said by more than one of the early Muslims. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us, Jaafar bin Awn told me, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mukhariq, on the authority of his father Al-Mukhariq bin Saleem, who said: Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him - said to us: If we narrate to you a hadith, we will bring you confirmation of that from the Book of God Almighty, “When the Muslim slave says, ‘Glory be to God and His praise, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, blessed be God,’ an angel takes them and places them under his wing, then ascends with them to the heavens, and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they ask forgiveness for the one who says them until he brings them with the face of God Almighty.” Then Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, recited, To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Sa’id Al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, have a buzz around the Throne like the buzzing of bees, reminding their speaker and righteous action in… Al-Khaza’in treasuries, and this is a sound chain of transmission going back to Ka’b al-Ahbar, may God have mercy on him, and it has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Musa - meaning Ibn Muslim Al-Tahhan - told us, on the authority of Awn Ibn Abdullah, on the authority of his father or his brother, on the authority of An-Nu’man Ibn Bashir, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Those who remember the majesty of God, by glorifying Him, praising Him, and declaring His oneness, gather around the Throne, making a buzz like the buzzing of bees, reminding one of their companion. Wouldn’t any of you like to always have something with God that reminds him of it?’” And thus Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bishr Khalaf, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan, on the authority of Musa Ibn Abi ‘Isa Al-Tahhan, on the authority of Awn Ibn Abdullah Ibn Utbah Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of his father or his brother, on the authority of An-Nu’man Ibn Bashir, may God be pleased with him, with it. God the Almighty said: And righteous action elevates it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Good speech is the remembrance of God, which ascends to God the Almighty. Good action is performing an obligatory duty. Whoever remembers God while performing his obligatory duties, his actions and remembrance of God will be attributed to God the Almighty. Whoever remembers God but does not perform his obligatory duties, his words will be rejected based on his actions, so he is more deserving of them. Mujahid also said: Good action is elevated by good speech. Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Shahr bin Hawshab and others said the same. Iyas bin Mu’awiyah Al-Qadi said: If it were not for good action, speech would not be elevated. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: No speech is accepted without action. And the Almighty said: And those who plot evil deeds Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair and Shahr bin Hawshab said: They are the hypocrites with their deeds, meaning they plot against people and give the impression that they are obeying God, the Most High, while they are hateful to God, the Most High, and they show off with their deeds. And they do not remember God except a little. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: They are the polytheists. The correct view is that it is general, and the polytheists are included by a fortiori, and for this reason God, the Most High, said: For them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those is bound to perish meaning it will be corrupted and nullified, and their falsehood will soon become apparent to those with insight and understanding. For no one conceals a secret except that God, the Most High, reveals it on the pages of his face and the slips of his tongue, and no one conceals a secret except that God, the Most High, clothes him in its cloak, whether good or evil. So the hypocrite’s affair does not spread and persist except to a fool. As for the discerning believers, it does not spread to them, rather it will be revealed to them soon, and nothing is hidden from the Knower of the Unseen. God the Almighty said: And God created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, meaning He began the creation of your father from dust, then made his offspring from a lineage of despised water. Then He made you mates, meaning male and female, as a kindness and mercy from Him that He made for you mates from among your kind so that you may find tranquility in them. God the Almighty said: And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge, meaning He knows all about that, nothing of it is hidden from Him. Rather, “not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And there is no grain within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is [written] in a clear register.” We have already discussed God the Almighty’s saying: “God knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb and [give], and everything with Him is by [determined] measure. * Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Most High.” And the Almighty said: And no one is granted a long life, nor is there any reduction in his lifespan, except that it is in a book. That is, what is given to some sperm of a long life, He knows it and it is with Him in the first book. And no one is granted a long lifespan, nor is there any reduction in his lifespan. The pronoun refers to the genus, not the entity, because a person who has a long lifespan is in the book and in the knowledge of Almighty God does not reduce his lifespan. Rather, the pronoun refers to the genus. Ibn Jarir said: This is like their saying, I have a garment and a half of it, meaning it is him and half of another garment. It was narrated by way of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the Almighty’s statement: “And no one is granted a long lifespan, nor is there any reduction in his lifespan, except that it is in a book. Indeed, that, for God, is easy.” He said: No one for whom You have decreed a long lifespan and life will reach the book that You have decreed, and You have decreed that for him. So he only reaches the book that You have decreed, and nothing will be added to it. And no one for whom You have decreed that his lifespan and life will reach the age, but he will reach the book that You have decreed. So that is the statement of Almighty God: “And no one is granted a long lifespan, except that it is in a book. Indeed, that, for God, is easy.” He said: All of that is in a book with Him. And this is what Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said on the authority of his father, And nothing is shortened from his lifespan except in a book. He said: The children that the wombs have expelled before they are complete. Abdul Rahman said in its interpretation: Don’t you see that people live a hundred years and another dies as he is born? This is this. Qatada said: And the one whose lifespan is shortened is the one who dies before the age of sixty. Mujahid said: And no one is granted a long lifespan or has his lifespan shortened except in a book. That is, in his mother’s womb, that is written for him. He was not created for one lifespan, but this one has a lifespan, and this one’s lifespan is less than his lifespan. So all of that is written for its owner, no matter how long he reaches it. Some of them said: Rather, its meaning is And no one is granted a long lifespan, that is, what is written of the term, nor is his lifespan shortened, which is his passing little by little. All of it is known to God, the Most High, year after year, month after month, Friday after Friday, day after day, and hour after hour. All of it is written with God, the Most High, in His book. Ibn Jarir transmitted it on the authority of Abu Malik, and Al-Suddi and Ata’ Al-Khurasani adopted this view. Ibn Jarir chose the first, and it is as he said. Al-Nasa’i said in his interpretation of this noble verse: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Zayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Ibn Wahb say: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever would like his provision to be expanded and his lifespan to be prolonged, let him maintain the ties of kinship.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Walid bin Al-Walid bin Abdul-Malik bin Ubaidullah Abu Sarh told us, Uthman bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Muslima bin Abdullah, on the authority of his paternal uncle Abu Mushaja bin Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ may God be pleased with him, who said: We were mentioned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: “God does not delay a soul when its appointed time has come. Rather, the extension of one’s lifespan is through righteous offspring that He grants to the servant, who will supplicate for him after him, and their supplications will reach him in his grave. That is the extension of one’s lifespan.” And the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, that, for God, is easy means it is easy for Him. His knowledge of that and its details is easy for Him in all of His creation, for His knowledge is comprehensive of all, and nothing of it is hidden from Him.
35:1: Interpretation of Surah Fatir It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I did not know what Fatir al-Samawat wa’l-Ard was until two Bedouins came to me disputing about a well. One of them said to his companion: I started it, meaning I began it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, also said: Fatir al-Samawat wa’l-Ard means Originator of the heavens and the earth. Ad-Dahhak said: Everything in the Qur’an is Fatir al-Samawat wa’l-Ard, meaning He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. And the Almighty’s saying: He has made the angels messengers meaning between Him and His prophets with wings meaning they fly with them to quickly convey what they are commanded to do in twos, threes, or fours meaning some of them have two wings, some have three, some have four, and some have more than that, as came in the hadith “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, on the night of the Isra’ and he had six hundred wings, between each two wings is like the distance between the east and the west.” And for this reason the Almighty said: “He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, God has power over all things.” Al-Suddi said: He increases in wings and their creation what He wills. Al-Zuhri and Ibn Jurayj said regarding the Almighty’s saying: He increases in creation what He wills meaning a beautiful voice. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Al-Zuhri in Al-Adab, and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir. And in the odd reading it was He increases in creation with a long ha’, and God knows best.
35:2: God the Almighty informs us that whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen, and that there is no one who can prevent what He gives and no one who can give what He prevents. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Asim told us, Mughira told us, Amir told us, on the authority of Warrad, the freed slave of Mughira bin Shu'ba, who said: Mu'awiyah wrote to Mughira bin Shu'ba, "Write for me what you heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)." Mughira called me and I wrote to him: "I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say when he finished the prayer: 'There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. O God, there is no one who can prevent what You give and no one who can give what You prevent. And wealth does not benefit one from You.' And I heard him forbid idle talk, excessive questioning, wasting wealth, burying daughters alive, disobeying mothers, and withholding and giving." And they narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Warrad. It was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri may God be pleased with him who said: “Whenever the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) raised his head from bowing, he would say: ‘God hears those who praise Him. O God, our Lord, to You is praise that fills the heavens and the earth, and that which You will thereafter. O God, the One worthy of praise and glory. What the servant has said is more true than what you have given, and we are all Your servants. O God, there is no one who can withhold what You have given, nor can there be a giver of what You have withheld. And wealth does not benefit a wealthy person against You.’” This verse is similar to the saying of God, the Most Blessed, the Most High: And if God should touch you with adversity, there is none who can remove it except Him; and if He intends for you good, there is none who can repel His favor. And there are many similar verses. Imam Malik may God have mercy on him said: When Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him was visited by rain, he would say: We have been rained upon by the star of victory. Then he would recite this verse: “Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it thereafter. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Ibn Wahb on his authority.
35:3: The Almighty warns His servants and guides them to prove His Oneness by singling out worship for Him alone, just as He is the One who is independent in creation and provision, so too should He be singled out for worship and not be associated with anyone else from idols, rivals, and statues. For this reason, the Almighty said: There is no god but He, so how are you deluded? That is, how can you be deluded after this clarification and the clarity of this proof, and after this you worship rivals and idols? And God knows best.
35:4: And the Blessed and Exalted says: And if these polytheists deny you, O Muhammad, and oppose you in what you have brought them of monotheism, then you have an example in the messengers who came before you, for they also came to their people with clear proofs and commanded them to monotheism, but they denied them and opposed them. And to God are all matters returned, meaning, We will reward them for that with the greatest reward. Then the Almighty said: O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true, meaning the Resurrection will inevitably happen. So let not the worldly life delude you, meaning, the lowly life in comparison to what God has prepared for His friends and followers of His messengers of great good, so do not be distracted from that everlasting by this transient flower. And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God, meaning Satan, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said, meaning, let not Satan tempt you and turn you away from following the messengers of God and believing in His words, for he is a deceitful, lying liar. This verse is like the verse at the end of Luqman 31:So let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you about God, and Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam is the devil, as the believers will say to the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection when they will be “put up between them a wall with a door, inside of which is mercy, but outside of it is torment. They will call out to them, “Were we not with you?” They will say, Yes, but you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted, and wishful thinking deceived you until the command of God came, and the Deceiver deceived you about God. Then God the Almighty explained the enmity of Satan to the son of Adam, saying: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. That is, he is a rival to you in enmity, so be his most intense enmity, oppose him, and deny what he deceives you with. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze. That is, he only intends to mislead you so that you enter with him into the punishment of the Blaze. This is the clear enemy. We ask God the Strong, the Almighty to make us enemies of Satan and to grant us the ability to follow the Book of God and to imitate the path of His Messengers. He is capable of whatever He wills and is worthy of answering. This is like His Almighty saying: “And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was one of the jinn and disobeyed the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are an enemy to you? An evil exchange for the wrongdoers.”

This is this. Qatada said: And the one whose lifespan is shortened is the one who dies before the age of sixty. Mujahid said: And no one is granted a long lifespan or has his lifespan shortened except in a book. That is, in his mother’s womb, that is written for him. Then they borrow in summer and winter. 35:27: God Almighty says, pointing out the perfection of His power in creating various and different things from one thing, which is the water that He sends down from the sky, with which He produces fruits of different colors, from yellow, red, green, white, and other colors of fruits, as is seen from the variety of their colors, tastes, and smells, as God Almighty said in another verse: “And on the earth are neighboring tracts and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, some of them twined and some untied, watered with one water. And We make some of them excel others in food. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.” And the saying of the Most High: And among the mountains are streaks white and red, of varying colors. That is, He created the mountains in this way, varying in color, as is also seen of white and red, and in some of them are paths, which are jadida the plural of jadda, also varying in color. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: The jadid are the paths, and so said Abu Malik, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi. And among them are qarabib black crows. Ikrimah said: The qarabib are the tall, black mountains. And so said Abu Malik, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir said: When the Arabs describe black as having a lot of blackness, they say: Aswad gharibib. For this reason, some of the commentators said about this verse: This is from the introduction and delay in the saying of the Most High: And black crows, meaning black as crows, and what he said is debatable. And the Almighty said: And among mankind and beasts and grazing livestock are different colors likewise. That is, likewise the animals, from mankind and beasts, which is everything that creeps on legs, and livestock, by way of connecting the specific to the general, likewise they are also different. So among people are Berbers, Abyssinians, and Tomatoes who are extremely black, and Slavs and Romans who are extremely white, and the Arabs are between that and the Indians less so. For this reason the Almighty said in the other verse: “And the diversity of your languages and colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.” And likewise the beasts and livestock are different colors, even within the same species, rather one type of them is different colors, rather one animal may have a speckled color of this color and that color, so blessed be God, the best of creators. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Al-Fadl ibn Sahl narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Abaan ibn Salih narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Does your Lord dye? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, a dye that will not be shaken off: red, yellow, and white.” It was narrated in mursal and mawquf forms, and God knows best. That is why God, the Most High, said after this: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. That is, only those who have knowledge of Him fear Him with the fear He should be truly feared, because the more knowledge of the Great, Powerful, All-Knowing One, who is described with attributes of perfection and described with the Most Beautiful Names, the more perfect and complete the knowledge of Him is, the greater and more intense the fear of Him will be. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge, he said: Those who know that God has power over all things. Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Ibn Abi Umrah on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “The one who has knowledge of the Most Merciful among His servants is the one who does not associate anything with Him, makes lawful what He has made lawful and forbids what He has forbidden, keeps His commandment, and is certain that he will meet Him and will be held accountable for his deeds.” Saeed bin Jubayr said: Fear is what stands between you and disobeying God Almighty. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The one who has knowledge is the one who fears the Most Merciful in the unseen, desires what God desires, and abstains from what God is displeased with. Then Al-Hasan recited: “Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud may God be pleased with him that he said: Knowledge is not achieved by many hadiths, but rather by much fear of God. Ahmad ibn Salih al-Masri narrated on the authority of Ibn Wahb that Malik said: Knowledge is not achieved by many narrations, rather knowledge is a light that God places in the heart. Ahmad ibn Salih al-Masri said: What it means is that fear of God is not attained by many narrations, rather the knowledge that God the Almighty has commanded to be followed is the Qur'an and the Sunnah and what was narrated from the Companions may God be pleased with them and the Imams of the Muslims who came after them. This can only be attained by narrating. The interpretation of his statement, "light," is to mean understanding knowledge and recognizing its meanings. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taimi that a man said: It was said that scholars are of three types: one who knows God, one who knows God's command, one who knows God's command but does not know God's command, and one who knows God's command but does not know God. The one who knows God and God's command is the one who fears God and knows the prescribed limits and obligations. The one who knows God but does not know God's command is the one who fears God but does not know the prescribed limits and obligations. The one who knows God's command is not the one who knows God's punishment and obligations but does not fear God the Almighty.

For this reason, He preferred the prophets and messengers over all of humanity, and He preferred some prophets over others, and He raised some of them in degrees and made the status of Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, above all of them, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all.
35:32: God the Almighty says: Then We made those who uphold the great Book, confirming what came before it of the Book, those whom We chose from among Our servants, and they are this nation. Then He divided them into three types, and God the Almighty said: Among them is he who wrongs himself meaning he is excessive in doing some of the obligatory acts and committing some of the forbidden acts. And among them is he who is moderate meaning he who performs the obligatory acts, leaves the forbidden acts, and may leave some of the recommended acts and do some of the disliked acts. And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God’s permission meaning he who does the obligatory and recommended acts, leaves the forbidden and disliked acts, and some of the permissible acts. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Then We caused those We chose of Our servants to inherit the Book, he said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God, the Most High, caused them to inherit every Book that He revealed. So the wrongdoer among them will be forgiven, the moderate among them will be given an easy reckoning, and the foremost among them will enter Paradise without being held to account. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya bin Uthman bin Salih and Abd al-Rahman bin Muawiyah al-Utbi told us: Abu al-Tahir bin al-Sarh told us, Musa bin Abd al-Rahman al-San’ani told us. Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said one day: My intercession is for the major sinners among my nation. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: “The one who is foremost in good deeds will enter Paradise without being brought to account, the moderate will enter Paradise by God’s mercy, and the one who wrongs himself and the people of A’raf will enter Paradise by the intercession of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was also narrated from more than one of the early Muslims that the one who wrongs himself from this nation is among the chosen ones, despite his crookedness and shortcomings. Others said: Rather, the one who wrongs himself is not from this nation nor among the chosen ones who inherit the Book.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Hashim ibn Marzuq told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Among them is he who wrongs himself, he said: He is the disbeliever. Ikrimah narrated this same thing from him, and Ikrimah also said the same in what Ibn Jarir narrated. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the verse: Among them is he who wrongs himself, he said: They are the people of the left. Malik said, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Hasan and Qatadah: He is the hypocrite. Then Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: “These three categories are like the three categories mentioned at the beginning and end of Surat al-Waqi’ah. The correct view is that the one who wrongs himself is from this ummah, and this is the preferred view of Ibn Jarir, as is apparent from the verse, and as it is reported in the hadiths from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) through chains of transmission that support each other. We, God willing, will cite from them what is easy.” The first hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Al-`Aizar, that he heard a man from Thaqeef narrating, on the authority of a man from Kinanah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), that he said concerning this verse: “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God’s permission.” He said: All of these will be of one status, and all of them will be in Paradise. This is a strange hadith from this source, and in its chain of transmission is someone who was not named. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it similarly from the hadith of Shu`bah. The meaning of his saying of one status is that they are from this nation, and they are among the people of Paradise, even if there is a difference in status between them in Paradise. The second hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Anas bin Ayyad al-Laithi Abu Damrah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Ali bin Abdullah al-Azdi, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God Almighty said: ‘Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God’s permission. As for those who are foremost, they are the ones who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. As for those who are moderate, they are the ones who will be brought to an easy account. As for those who wronged themselves, they are the ones who will be detained for a long time on the Day of Resurrection. Then they are the ones whom God will meet with His mercy. They are the ones who will say: ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative. * Who has settled us in the home of eternity out of His bounty. No toil will touch us therein, nor will weariness touch us therein.’” Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: Asid bin Asim told us, Al-Husayn bin Hafs told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Thabit, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those We chose from among Our servants. Among them are those who wrong themselves.” He said: As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained until he is afflicted with worry and sadness, then he will enter Paradise. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan Al-Thawri on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Abu Thabit mentioned that he entered the mosque and sat next to Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, and said: O God, comfort my loneliness, have mercy on my estrangement, and make a righteous companion easy for me. Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, said: “If you are truthful, then I am happier with you than you. I will tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which I have not told since I heard it from him.” He mentioned this verse: “Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those We chose from among Our servants. Among them are those who wrong themselves, and among them are those who are moderate, and among them are those who foremost.” With good deeds. As for the one who is foremost in good deeds, he will enter them without being held accountable. As for the moderate one, he will be held to account with a light accounting. As for the one who is unjust to himself, he will be afflicted in that place with grief and sadness, and that is what God Almighty says: And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow.’ The third hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas told us, Ibn Masoud told us, Sahl bin Abd Rabbih Al-Razi told us, Amr bin Abi Qais told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of his brother, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, may God be pleased with them both: And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of God [the verse]. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of them are from this nation. The Fourth Hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Aziz told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Awf bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “My nation is divided into three parts: a third will enter Paradise without being held to account or punished, a third will be held to a light reckoning and then enter Paradise, and a third will be tested and revealed, then the angels will come and say, ‘We found them saying, ‘There is no god but God alone.’ God Almighty will say, ‘They have spoken the truth, there is no god but Me.’ Enter Paradise because of their saying, ‘There is no god but God alone,’ and carry their sins on the people of Hellfire.” This is what God Almighty said: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens besides their burdens. The confirmation of this is in the one in which the angels are mentioned. God Almighty said: Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants. So He made them three types, and they are all classes. Some of them are unjust to themselves, so this one who is tested and revealed is very strange. On the authority of Ibn Masoud may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told me, Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Abdullah bin Isa, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Shaqiq Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: “This nation will be divided into three thirds on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a third will enter Paradise without being held to account, a third will be held to a light account, and a third will come with great sins until God, the Almighty, says: Who are these? And He, the Blessed and Exalted, knows best. Then the angels will say: These have come with great sins, except that they did not associate anything with You. Then the Almighty Lord will say: Admit these people into the breadth of My mercy.” Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, recited this verse: Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those We have chosen of Our servants. Another trace Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said on the authority of al-Salt bin Dinar bin al-Ash’ath on the authority of Uqbah bin Sahban al-Hana’i who said: I asked Aisha, may God be pleased with her, about the saying of God Almighty: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We chose of Our servants, and among them is he who wrongs himself 1:13. She said to me: “O my son, these are in Paradise. As for the one who is foremost in good deeds, he is the one who lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, testified to his life and provision. As for the moderate one, he is the one who followed in his footsteps from his companions until he caught up with him. As for the one who is unjust to himself, he is like me and you.” He said: So she made herself, may God be pleased with her, with us. This from her, may God be pleased with her, is from the perspective of tolerance and humility. Otherwise, she is one of the greatest of those who are foremost in good deeds because her superiority over women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods. Abdullah bin Mubarak, may God have mercy on him, said: The Commander of the Faithful, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, said regarding the words of God Almighty: And among them is he who wrongs himself, he said: It is for the people of the desert and the moderate people of the cities and the forerunners of the people of jihad. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Aouf Al-A'rabi said: Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal told us: Kaab Al-Ahbar, may God have mercy on him, told us: The one from this nation who wrongs himself, the moderate, and the one who is foremost in good deeds are all in Paradise. Have you not seen that God, the Most High, said: "Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God's permission. That is the great bounty. Gardens of perpetual bliss which they will enter." until His saying, the Most High, the Most Majestic, And those who disbelieve will have the fire of Hell. He said: These are the people of Hell. Ibn Jarir narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Aouf. Then he said: Ya'qub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Al-Harith on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, asked Kaab about the words of God, the Most High: "Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God's permission." He said: Their shoulders touched, and by the Lord of Kaab, then they were given bounty for their deeds. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Subaie, regarding this verse: Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We chose of Our servants 1:13. Abu Ishaq said: As for what you heard from the sixty-year-old, all of them will be saved. Then he said: Ibn Humayd told us, Al-Hakam told us, Amr told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, may God be pleased with him, who said: It is a nation that is shown mercy. The oppressor is forgiven, the moderate one is in Paradise with God, and the one who is foremost in good deeds is in ranks with God. And Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Sami’, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, may God be pleased with him, in a similar manner. Abu al-Jarud said: I asked Muhammad ibn Ali - meaning al-Baqir - may God be pleased with them both, about the statement of God the Most High: And among them is he who wrongs himself. He said: He is the one who mixes a righteous deed with another that is evil. This is what was possible to cite from the hadiths and narrations related to this matter. Once this is established, the verse is general and applies to all three categories of this nation. The scholars are the most envied people for this blessing and the most deserving of this mercy, for they are as Imam Ahmad - may God have mercy on him - said: Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, Asim ibn Raja’ ibn Haywah told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Kathir, who said: A man from the people of Madinah came to Abu al-Darda’ - may God be pleased with him - while he was in Damascus. He said: What brought you here, my brother? He said: “A hadith that I have heard that you narrate from the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace.” He said: Did you not come for trade? He said: No. He said: Did you not come for a need? He said: No. He said: Did you come only to seek this hadith? He said: Yes. He, may God be pleased with him, said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge, God Almighty will make easy for him a path to Paradise. The angels lower their wings in satisfaction with the seeker of knowledge. Everyone in the heavens and the earth, even the fish in the water, seeks forgiveness for the scholar. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon over all the planets. The scholars are the heirs of the prophets. The prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams, but they left behind knowledge. So whoever takes it has taken a great portion.’” Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Katheer ibn Qays. Some of them say Qays ibn Katheer on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him. We have mentioned its chains of transmission and the differences among the narrators in the explanation of the Book of Knowledge in Sahih al-Bukhari, praise and thanks be to God. At the beginning of Surah Taha, there is the hadith of Tha’laba ibn al-Hakam, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty will say to the scholars on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:I did not place My knowledge and wisdom among you except that I wanted to forgive you for what you did.” I don't care.
35:33: God the Almighty informs us that the abode of these chosen ones from among His servants who have inherited the Book revealed from the Lord of the Worlds on the Day of Resurrection will be the Gardens of Eden, meaning the Gardens of Eternity, which they will enter on the Day of Resurrection and their arrival before God the Almighty. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, as proven in the Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said, The adornment of the believer will reach as far as the ablution reaches. “And their clothing therein will be silk.” For this reason, it was forbidden to them in this world, but God the Almighty permitted it for them in the Hereafter. It is proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter, and he said, It is for them in this world and for you in the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Suwad al-Sarhi told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Aqil ibn Khalid, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them, and he mentioned the adornments of the people of Paradise, and he said: “They will be encrusted with gold and silver, crowned with pearls, and they will have wreaths of pearls and rubies, one after the other, and they will have crowns like the crowns of kings, young, beardless, kohl-rimmed men. And they will say: ‘Praise be to God, who has taken away from us sorrow’” meaning the fear of something forbidden. He has removed it from us and relieved us of what we feared and warned against of the worries of this world and the hereafter. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no loneliness for the people of ‘There is no god but God’ in their graves or in the resurrection. It is as if I see the people of ‘There is no god but God’ shaking the dust off their heads and saying: ‘Praise be to God who has removed sorrow from us.’” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from his hadith. Al-Tabarani said: Ja’far bin Muhammad Al-Faryabi told us, Musa bin Yahya Al-Marwazi told us, Sulayman bin Abdullah bin Wahb Al-Kufi told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Hakim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no loneliness for the people of ‘La ilaha illa God’ in death, nor in the graves, nor in the resurrection. It is as if I see them at the shout, shaking the dust off their heads, saying: ‘Praise be to God, who has removed sorrow from us. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.’” Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and others said: He forgave them many of their sins, and thanked them for the little good deeds. Who has settled us in the abode of eternity out of His bounty. They say: He who gave us this status and this station out of His bounty, grace, and mercy. Our deeds were not equal to that, as was proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of you will enter Paradise because of his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God Almighty covers me with His mercy and grace. “No fatigue will touch us therein, nor will any hardship touch us therein.” Laghoob means that we will not be touched by any hardship or fatigue therein. Both nasb and laghoob are used to indicate fatigue, and it seems that what is meant by negating this and that from them is that they will not be tired or exhausted in their bodies or souls, and God knows best. From that is that they used to devote themselves to worship in this world, so the obligation to enter it was dropped from them, and they were in constant, continuous rest. God Almighty said: Eat and drink at ease for what you put forth in the past days.

35:36: When the Blessed and Exalted mentioned the state of the happy ones, He began to explain the fate of the wretched ones, saying: “And those who disbelieve will have the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed to die, nor will they live therein.” Just as the Almighty said: He neither dies therein nor lives. It is proven in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for the people of Hell who are its people, they will neither die therein nor live. And the Almighty said: And they will call, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us.’ He will say, ‘Indeed, you will remain.’ So in that state, they see their death as a relief for them, but there is no way to do that. God the Almighty said: They will not be decreed to die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Just as the Almighty said: “Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally. It will not be relieved for them, and therein they will be in despair.” And the Almighty said: Whenever it subsides, We will increase their blazing fire. “So taste [it], for We will not increase you except in punishment.” Then the Almighty said: Thus do We recompense every ungrateful person. That is, this is the recompense of everyone who… He disbelieved in his Lord and denied the truth. And His statement, may He be glorified: And they will cry out therein, meaning they will call out therein, crying out to God Almighty with their voices, Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do, meaning they will ask to return to this world so that they may do other than their first work. And the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, knows that if He were to return them to this worldly abode, they would return to what they were forbidden from, and they are indeed liars. He will reward every worker according to his deeds. Then He the Almighty said, It is He who has made you successors upon the earth, meaning He will replace one people with another before them and one generation with another. As God the Almighty said, And will make you successors on the earth, "So whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief," meaning the consequences of that will only be upon himself and no one else. "And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in the sight of their Lord except in hatred," meaning the more they persist in their disbelief, the more God the Almighty hates them, and the more they persist in it, they will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, unlike the believers, for the longer a person lives and the better his deeds, the higher his status and position in Paradise, the greater his reward, and the more his Creator and Maker, the Lord of the Worlds, loves him.
35:40: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the polytheists: Have you seen your partners whom you invoke besides God? That is, idols and rivals, Show me what they have created on earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? That is, they do not have any of that, as they own even a date stone. And His statement, Or have We given them a Scripture from which they are clear? That is, or have We sent down to them a Scripture containing what they say of polytheism and disbelief? The matter is not like that. Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion. That is, rather, they only followed their whims, opinions, and desires that they desire for themselves, which are delusion, falsehood, and lies. Then the Almighty informed us of His great power by which the heavens and the earth stand by His command, and of the power He placed in them to hold them together. He said, Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist, meaning that they should move from their places, as the Almighty said, And He holds the heaven lest it fall upon the earth except by His permission, and the Almighty said, And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command, “And if they should cease, no one could hold them back after Him,” meaning that no one is able to sustain them and keep them alive except Him. And He is, in addition to that, Forbearing and Forgiving, meaning that He sees His servants while they disbelieve in Him and disobey Him, and He is Forbearing, so He delays, and He watches and postpones, but does not hasten, and He conceals others and forgives. For this reason the Almighty said, Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here a strange, even objectionable, hadith. He said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham bin Yusuf told me, on the authority of Umayyah bin Shibl, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, narrating from Moses, peace be upon him, on the pulpit. He said: It occurred to Moses, peace be upon him, ‘Does God Almighty sleep?’ So God sent an angel to him who made him sleep three days, and gave him two bottles, one in each hand, and ordered him to take care of them. He said: So he would sleep, and his hands would almost meet, then he would wake up and hold one of them back from the other until he fell asleep, and his hands clapped together and the two bottles broke. He said: God gave him an example that if God Almighty were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not hold together.” It appears that this hadith is not attributed to the Prophet, peace be upon him, but rather is one of the objectionable Isra’iliyyat, because Moses, peace be upon him, is too lofty to be mentioned by God, glory be to Him. Sleep, and God Almighty has informed us in His Noble Book that He is “the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.” It is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty does not sleep, and it is not befitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the balance and raises it, and the deeds of the night are raised to Him before those of the day, and the deeds of the day before those of the night. His veil is light or fire. Were He to remove it, the glory of His face would burn up everything that His sight reaches of His creation.” Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, `Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A`mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: A man came to `Abdullah, that is, Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him, and said: Where did you come from? He said: From Ash-Sham. He said: Whom did you meet? He said: I met Ka`b. He said: What did he tell you? He said: He told me that the heavens revolve on the shoulder of an angel. He said: Did you believe him or disbelieve him? He said: I neither believed him nor disbelieved him. He said: I would have liked to have been ransomed from your journey to him by your mount and its saddle. Ka`b lied, for God the Almighty says: “Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. And if they should cease, no one could hold them back after Him.” This is a sound chain of transmission going back to Ka`b and to Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid on the authority of Jarir on the authority of Mughira on the authority of Ibrahim who said: Jundub Al-Bajali went to Ka’b in Ash-Sham and he mentioned something similar. I have seen in a book by the jurist Yahya bin Ibrahim bin Muzain Al-Talaitili entitled Siyar Al-Fuqaha that he included this trace on the authority of Muhammad bin Isa bin Al-Tabba’ on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. Then he said: And Zunan informed us, meaning Abdul Malik bin Al-Hasan on the authority of Ibn Wahb on the authority of Malik that he said: The sky does not rotate, and he used as evidence this verse and the hadith, Indeed, in the West there is a door to repentance that will remain open until the sun rises from it. I said: This hadith is in the Sahih, and God knows best.

35:42: God the Almighty tells us about the Quraysh and the Arabs, that they swore by God with the strongest oaths before sending the Messenger to them, If a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the nations, meaning, of all the nations to which the Messengers were sent. Ad-Dahhak and others said this, as God the Almighty said: “That you should not say, ‘The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and that we were, of their study, unaware.’ Or that you should say, ‘If only the Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than them.’ But there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord and guidance and mercy. So who is more unjust than he who denies the verses of God and turns away from them?” And as God the Almighty said: And indeed, they used to say, ‘If only we had had a reminder from among the former peoples,’ we would have been the chosen servants of God.’ But they disbelieved in him, and they are going to know. God the Almighty said: But when there came to them a warner, that is, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, with what was sent down with him of the great Book, which is the clear Qur’an, it only increased them in aversion, meaning they only increased in disbelief to their disbelief. Then He explained this by saying: Arrogance in the land meaning: they were too arrogant to follow the signs of God. And evil plotting meaning: they plotted against people to turn them away from the path of God. And evil plotting does not encompass except its own people meaning: the consequences of that do not come back to anyone except themselves, not to anyone else. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein mentioned, Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Zakariya Al-Kufi, on the authority of a man who told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of evil plotting, for evil plotting only encompasses its people, and they will be pursued by God. Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: There are three things that whoever does them will not be saved until it befalls him: plotting, transgressing, or breaking the covenant. The confirmation of these is in the Book of God, the Most High: And evil plotting only encompasses its people. “Your transgression is only against yourselves.” So whoever breaks his covenant only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And the words of God, the Most High: Do they then await anything but the way of the former peoples? Meaning, God’s punishment for them for denying His messengers and disobeying His command? And you will not find any change in the way of God. That is, it does not change or alter, rather it is thus applied to every denier. And you will not find any alteration in the way of God. That is, And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it. No one can remove that from them or change it from them. And God knows best.

35:44: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those who denied the message you brought them: Travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied the messengers, how God destroyed them and the disbelievers like them, so their homes became empty of them, and they were robbed of the comforts they had been in after their complete strength and great numbers, and the abundance of wealth and children. But that did not avail them at all, nor did it ward off anything from God’s punishment, when the command of your Lord came, because nothing is beyond His power if He wills to be in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is All-Knowing and All-Powerful. That is, He is All-Knowing of all beings and All-Powerful over all of them. Then God Almighty said: And if God were to punish people for what they have earned, He would not leave on the back of the earth any creature. That is, if He were to punish them for all their sins, He would destroy all the people of the earth and all the creatures and provisions they own. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The dung beetle was almost tormented in its hole because of the sin of Adam’s son. Then he recited: And if God were to punish men for what they have earned, He would not have left upon the earth’s back any creature. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said regarding the verse: He would not have left upon the earth’s back any creature, meaning when He gave them rain and all the creatures died, but He defers them for a specified term, meaning, He gives them respite until the Day of Resurrection, when He will hold them to account, and He will fully pay for every worker’s deeds, rewarding the obedient with reward and punishing the disobedient. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: And when their term comes, then indeed, God is ever, of His servants, Seeing. End of the interpretation of Surah Fatir. All praise and thanks are due to God.
